subject: RApache Configure Does Not Recognize R Installed with Shared Library

messages.author: cf41d031ab177789
messages.subject: RApache Configure Does Not Recognize R Installed with Shared Library
parts:
All: Apologies in advance for what I hope is an easy question. It's
been many years since I've worked in a Unix(-like) environment...

I'm trying to install RApache on a web server running the RHEL5 64-bit
OS. I've successfully installed Apache and confirmed it works. I've
also successfully installed R (R-2.13.0) with shared library. I've
confirmed that libBlas.so and libR.so are installed; location: /R/
R-2.13.0/lib

However, when I try to configure RApache ( sudo ./configure --with-
apache2-apxs=/usr/local/apache2/bin/ --with-R=/R/R-2.13.0/) I get the
following error:

R was not built as a shared library
Either build it with one, or use another install of R
configure: error: aborting!

I've reinstalled R twice now and have confirmed in libtool that it
says:

# Whether or not to build shared libraries.
build_libtool_libs=yes

Finally, I've searched high and low for some path or flag I need to
set without success. Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks, Ron

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: RApache Configure Does Not Recognize R Installed with Shared Library
parts:
You're almost there! You just need to specify the FULL path to the
apxs tool and the FULL path to R, not the install dir. This is
explained in the manual here:

http://www.rapache.net/manual.html#Running_configure

So in your case, you will want to call configure like so:

sudo ./configure --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/local/apache2/bin/apxs2 --
with-R=/R/R-2.13.0/bin/R

You might have to jigger that a bit, though, as I'm not positive
that's the right name of the apxs tool. It might just be 'apxs'.

Best,

Jeff

You've run into the famous .la issue. If you read those files (yes,
they're just text files), then you'll see that it contains various
paths to libraries that the .la depends on. You'll have to fix the .la
file to proceed, or find an updated rpm.

Best,

Jeff

Hi Jeff at al: Well, I guess I've got to holler uncle. I've played
with the /usr/lib/libexpat.la entries every way I can think of without
success. The issue may have something to do with the fact that on my
system the /usr/lib.libexpat.so file is a link to the file /lib/
libexpat.so.0.5.0 (though as you'll read below, I replaced the link
without success too). Here's the .la file:

# libexpat.la - a libtool library file
# Generated by ltmain.sh - GNU libtool 1.4.2 (1.922.2.53 2001/09/11
03:18:52)
#
# Please DO NOT delete this file!
# It is necessary for linking the library.

# The name that we can dlopen(3).
#dlname='libexpat.so.0'

# Names of this library.
library_names='libexpat.so.0.5.0 libexpat.so.0 libexpat.so'

# The name of the static archive.
old_library='libexpat.a'

# Libraries that this one depends upon.
dependency_libs=''

# Version information for libexpat.
current=5
age=5
revision=0

# Is this an already installed library?
installed=yes

# Files to dlopen/dlpreopen
dlopen=''
dlpreopen=''

# Directory that this library needs to be installed in:
libdir='/usr/lib'

I've changed both the libdir variable and the dlname variable to point
to all possible combinations of the .so, .so.0, and .so.0.5.0 files,
as well as the /usr/lib, /lib, and /usr/lib64 directories. I've even
gone so far as to copy the libexpat.so.0.5.0 file over the link to it
in the /usr/lib directory (renaming it to libexpat.so) without
success.

That is, the path changes do affect the error in the sense that the
path in the error message changes, but I always get the error ".../
libexpat.so: could not read symbols: File in wrong format". At this
point I've run out of things to try...

Here are what my directories look like (after I overwrote the link in
the /usr/lib directory):

Any other ideas? At this point I don't know what else to do besides
throw in the towel...

Best,
Ron

messages.subject: Re: RApache Configure Does Not Recognize R Installed with Shared Library
parts:
Try symlinking /usr/lib/libexpat.la to /usr/lib64/libexpat.la. your building 64 bit binaries but trying to link against a 32 bit libexpat.
